question.text: India deposited its MLI instrument of ratification with the OECD on 25 June 2019 and notified provisions effective 1 October 2019. In the context of treaty benefits available to non-resident investors in a Cat III AIF, MLI principally introduces:

answer.text: A Principal Purpose Test (PPT) and / or Limitation of Benefits (LOB) clauses
A blanket denial of treaty benefits to all non-residents
A mandatory 20% TDS on all treaty countries
A replacement of Section 115UB with Section 115UA

explanation.text: The Logic: MLI Action 15 of BEPS and Article 7 of the MLI implement anti-abuse rules, principally the Principal Purpose Test (PPT) and optionally a simplified LOB. Treaty benefits are denied if obtaining the benefit was one of the principal purposes of the arrangement unless benefit is in accordance with the object and purpose of the relevant treaty provision. The Trap: B is an absurd over-statement. C is not an MLI output; TDS rates are ITA. D mixes up Section 115UB (Cat I/II AIF) with 115UA (business trusts like REITs/InvITs). Cross-Exam Context: X-A/X-B test PPT and LOB for cross-border advisory. XIX-E frames it for Cat III NR LPs. XXIV (AML) overlaps on beneficial-ownership analysis. XV (Research Analyst) is not a direct hit. Manager's Pro-Tip: When bringing in a Singapore or Netherlands LP, run a preliminary PPT test — would the investor have chosen this vehicle absent the treaty benefit? Maintain contemporaneous commercial-substance files; a reactive PPT defence 3 years later is painful.
